report.summary: Chunk 4 of 5: defines select_backend, live registry, cancel_all_managed, and ManagedProcess.__init__; sets BACKEND and BACKEND_NAME at module level.
risks: select_backend | low | Uses platform.startswith("win") which matches 'win32' or 'win64', but also hypothetical 'win' prefix; but that's fine as it's a common pattern. | No risk, just observation.
_LIVE | medium | WeakSet may not immediately remove entries if the object is kept alive elsewhere; but that's expected behavior. | No action needed.
cancel_all_managed | medium | Catches Exception (BLE001 suppressed) silently; may hide bugs. | Consider logging or re-raising after collection.
ManagedProcess.__init__ | medium | If after_spawn fails, process is killed and waited with timeout 5; if kill fails, wait may hang? But it's in except, so safe. | No action needed.

handoff.purpose: Define backend selection, live process registry, emergency cancellation, and ManagedProcess class init.

symbols.name: select_backend
symbols.note: Returns WindowsJobBackend if platform starts with 'win', else PosixSessionBackend.

symbols.name: BACKEND
symbols.note: Module-level instance of the selected backend class.

symbols.name: BACKEND_NAME
symbols.note: Name of the backend class (e.g., 'WindowsJobBackend' or 'PosixSessionBackend').

symbols.name: _LIVE
symbols.note: WeakSet of ManagedProcess instances, protected by _LIVE_LOCK.

symbols.name: live_managed_processes
symbols.note: Returns list of ManagedProcess objects with returncode None.

symbols.name: cancel_all_managed
symbols.note: Calls cancel on each live process; default grace_s=0.0; never raises.

symbols.name: ManagedProcess
symbols.note: Context manager for a child process tree; supports cancellation and container release.

symbols.name: ManagedProcess.__init__
symbols.note: Initializes with argv, optional cwd/env/stdin/stdout/stderr/backend; spawns subprocess and registers it.

claims.text: Pick the containment backend for a platform string (``sys.platform``). Split out as a pure function so the platform decision is assertable from either OS without spawning anything.
claims.why: The function takes a string and returns a class; no side effects. The docstring accurately describes it.

claims.text: A WeakSet, so registration cannot keep a finished process object alive and cannot leak; entries are also discarded eagerly on close().
claims.why: The chunk does not define close() on ManagedProcess; the claim about eager discard on close() cannot be verified.

claims.text: Snapshot of every contained child alive in THIS interpreter.
claims.why: The function returns a list of processes from _LIVE where returncode is None.

claims.text: Cancel every live :class:`ManagedProcess` tree. Returns what each did. Never raises: one wedged child must not stop the rest from being killed. The default grace is 0.0, not :data:`DEFAULT_GRACE_S` -- this is the emergency path, where the whole point is to be fast, and a child that would have exited politely within three seconds is no less dead for being killed now.
claims.why: The function iterates over live processes, catches exceptions, and returns results. Default grace_s=0.0. Does not raise.

claims.text: A child process whose whole tree can be cancelled. Use as a context manager; leaving the block cancels anything still running and then releases the container. Dropping the last reference also releases the container, which on win32 kills any survivor -- an orphaned ``ManagedProcess`` must not leave writers behind.
claims.why: The chunk does not include __enter__, __exit__, or __del__; context manager behavior and last reference release cannot be verified.

claims.text: Registered ONLY here: after containment is established. A process we failed to contain is killed above and must never appear in a registry
claims.why: The chunk ends before the registration code; the claim cannot be verified.

observations.what: select_backend uses platform.startswith("win") to match Windows, which is correct for sys.platform values like 'win32' or 'win64'.
_LIVE is a WeakSet; the comment says entries are discarded eagerly on close(), but close() is not defined in this chunk.
cancel_all_managed catches Exception silently (BLE001 suppressed); this may hide errors.
ManagedProcess.__init__ has a complex error path: if after_spawn fails, it kills the process and waits with timeout 5; if that also fails, it silently passes.
The chunk ends before registering the process into _LIVE; the claim about registration only after containment is uncheckable in this chunk.
